title: GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket: issues, pull requests and code review

videos.script: Everything so far has been Git, the program on your machine. This lesson is about the website most teams keep their shared copy on. GitHub, GitLab or Bitbucket. {{sites}} They all add the same two things Git does not have. {{two}} The first is somewhere to write work down before it starts. An issue. A title, a description, a number, and somebody it is assigned to. {{issue}} The second is somewhere to talk about a change before it joins main. A pull request. {{pr}} And here is the idea that makes a pull request simple. It is not a new kind of thing. It is a branch, with a conversation attached. The page shows what the branch would change, the people reviewing it comment on the lines, and the branch keeps moving until they agree. {{branch}} Then somebody presses merge, and one of three things happens to the history, depending on the button. {{buttons}} The buttons will look different on every site, and they will look different next year. What they do will not. That is what this lesson is about. {{title}}
